name: n8nClaw
vibe_summary: A no-code reimagining of OpenClaw built entirely as a single n8n visual workflow, wiring Telegram, WhatsApp, and Gmail into a Claude-powered agent with Postgres memory and Supabase RAG. It trades OpenClaw's local runtime for drag-and-drop composability on top of n8n's automation ecosystem.
best_for: n8n users who want an OpenClaw-style assistant without writing code
Teams already running n8n, Postgres, and Supabase infrastructure
Rapid prototyping of multi-channel AI assistants
avoid_if: You need a true local-first agent with sandboxed execution
You want a mature, versioned product with releases and tests
You avoid depending on multiple external APIs (OpenRouter, Evolution, OpenAI)
openclaw_advantages: Visual, editable workflow instead of a code runtime
Leverages n8n's large integration library out of the box
Built-in multi-channel triggers (Telegram, WhatsApp, Gmail) with minimal config
Tiered worker sub-agents and scheduled memory summarization included
openclaw_disadvantages: Depends on n8n plus multiple cloud APIs rather than running locally
No sandboxing or execution isolation guarantees
Very young project: two commits, no releases, no license
No community discussion or independent reviews found
confidence_summary: Evidence is limited to the README, two initial commits, and generic OpenClaw-ecosystem web results with zero direct mentions of this project. Assessments of security, stability, and community sentiment are therefore low-confidence inferences.

overview_markdown:
n8nClaw is a lightweight, self-hosted AI assistant implemented entirely as an [n8n](https://n8n.io) visual workflow, positioned as a lite alternative to OpenClaw. Instead of a compiled runtime, the whole agent — triggers, routing, memory, and tools — lives in a single importable n8n workflow, making it approachable for no-code and automation-oriented users.

Architecturally, it fans in from multiple channel triggers (Telegram, WhatsApp via Evolution API, Gmail polling, and an hourly autonomous heartbeat), normalizes messages, and routes them through a central AI agent node powered by Claude Sonnet 4.5 via OpenRouter with a 15-message Postgres chat memory. A configurable 'soul' field defines personality, and a living user-profile document personalizes responses. Replies are switched back out over the originating channel.

Where it differs most from OpenClaw is its tool and memory layer: tiered worker sub-agents, task/subtask databases, email and document managers, and a scheduled memory pipeline that aggregates chat history, summarizes it with Haiku 4.5, embeds it with OpenAI, and stores it in a Supabase vector store for RAG. The trade-off is heavy reliance on external services and n8n itself, plus the project is brand new — two commits, no releases, and no declared license — so production readiness is unproven.
